decision.author: ezyang
decision.body:
Requesting changes — two correctness issues. (The `sm_107`/Rubin premise itself checks out; note at the bottom.)

### 1. `torch/_inductor/codegen/cutlass/utils.py` — `_gen_ops_cached` clobbers `manifest_arch`, regressing SM103

```python
gen_arch = "100" if arch == "103" or arch == "107" else arch
manifest_arch = "103a" if arch == "103" else gen_arch
manifest_arch = "107a" if arch == "107" else gen_arch   # <- unconditionally reassigns
```

The third line reassigns `manifest_arch` in its `else` branch for every non-`107` arch, discarding the `103a` set on the line above. For `arch == "103"`:

1. `gen_arch = "100"`
2. `manifest_arch = "103a"`
3. `arch != "107"` → `manifest_arch = gen_arch = "100"`

So SM103 ends up with `manifest_arch = "100"` instead of `"103a"`, which defeats the arch-conditional-kernel skipping that the adjacent comment says is required ("the CUTLASS manifest must keep the 103a feature arch so unsupported arch-conditional kernels are skipped"). The new `107` path works, but `103` is now broken. Suggest collapsing into a single chain, e.g.:

```python
if arch in ("103", "107"):
    gen_arch = "100"
    manifest_arch = f"{arch}a"
else:
    gen_arch = manifest_arch = arch
```

### 2. `cmake/Modules_CUDA_fix/upstream/FindCUDA/select_compute_arch.cmake` — `VERSION_GREATER "13.4"` excludes CUDA 13.4 itself

```cmake
if(CUDA_VERSION VERSION_GREATER "13.4")
```

`VERSION_GREATER` is a strict comparison, so this only fires on CUDA ≥ 13.5 — but the PR description says CUDA 13.4 is what adds Rubin, so building with 13.4 itself won't pick up the `Rubin`/`10.7` archs. Compare the neighboring Blackwell block, which gates on the release *before* introduction (`VERSION_GREATER "12.6"` for archs that landed in 12.8), and `cmake/Codegen.cmake`, which uses `VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL` for its per-arch gates. Suggest `VERSION_GREATER "13.3"` or `VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL "13.4"`.

---

**Premise check (FYI, not a change request):** the `sm_107 == Rubin` mapping holds up — the CUDA 13.4 developer-preview PTX ISA (9.4) release notes explicitly add `sm_107`, `sm_107f`, and `sm_107a` targets. The existence of the `sm_107f` *family* variant is also consistent with `sm_107` living in the `sm_100` (10.x) family, which is what justifies reusing the SM100 generator / `+PTX` handling here.

<sub>Disclosure: this review was prepared with AI assistance (Claude) and checked by me before posting.</sub>
